Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and the wake-visual inspection skill, then inspect current/inherited rollout evidence before touching the controller. I’ll keep all work inside this Phase 2 workspace and will not look for the omitted research shelf.

The wake-visual skill applies because the sampled examples include keyframe sheets; it requires comparing the strongest finite run with an informative failure and cross-checking images against metrics before any policy edit. I’m following that sequence now.

The rollout evidence already shows a clean local comparison: steering gain 1.7 reaches the target 1.61 time units sooner than gain 1.5, with lower mean distance, relative crossflow, force, moment, and command effort. I’m now checking the inherited failed variants and their visuals so the next change isolates one supported axis rather than mixing mechanisms.

Visual and numerical checks agree: the 1.7-gain fish makes the same self-propelled diagonal traverse as 1.5 but closes sooner and with slightly smaller wake/load excursions; the inherited multi-signal slow controller destabilizes almost immediately before meaningful progress. I’ll record the candidate hypothesis first, then make the conservative one-axis continuation to gain 1.9.

The candidate and durable experience bank are now updated. The reusable lesson records the validated bearing mechanism, the 1.5→1.7 matched improvement, and the inherited mixed-feedback instability boundary; the candidate changes only the near-zero steering gain to 1.9. I’m running the mandated workspace checker next.

The first mandated check found a duplicated identical “copied to guidance” parent marker in the rendered workspace README, so it cannot resolve the assigned parent. This is the same metadata defect recorded in inherited worker logs; I’ll remove only the duplicate marker and rerun the check.

The guidance-materiality and solver-boundary checks pass. The Julia runtime is absent in this workspace, so the exact executable smoke check cannot run; I’m compensating with the deterministic parameter-reference guard and an exact diff against the already CFD-evaluated 1.7 policy.

Produced exactly one candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_2d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1) — increases only `steering_gain` from `1.7` to `1.9`.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) — visual diagnosis and falsifiable hypothesis.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:1) — materially revised reusable lesson.

Guidance materiality, parameter schema, and solver boundary checks pass. Julia smoke testing was unavailable because `julia` is not installed; the policy differs from the evaluated 1.7 candidate by only the gain value. No CFD was run.
